body.heading: Make your theatre
paragraphs: Ask your adult to hang a plain sheet or find a bare wall. Turn the lights down and stand a lamp or torch behind you, pointing at the wall.
Your adult stays in charge of the lamp. Lamps can get warm, so only grown-ups move it.

body.heading: Make shadow animals
paragraphs: Hold your hands between the light and the wall. Link your thumbs and wiggle your fingers to make a flying bird.
Try a dog, a rabbit with long ears, or a waving monster. Move closer to the light to make the shadow bigger, and further away to make it smaller.

body.heading: Tell a tiny story
paragraphs: Invent a short story with two shadow characters. One can be lost, and the other can help it find its way home.
Swap roles and tell the story again a different way. There is no score and no wrong version.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: use a lamp, a wall, and your hands to put on a shadow puppet show.

safetyNotes: Only the adult handles the lamp or torch, because lamps can get hot; never shine a light into anyone's eyes.
Keep the play area clear so nobody trips in the dim light.
screenFreeExtension: Cut no shapes at all: use toys and teddies as shadow actors and let their shadows tell the next story.
